results.bound: \mathrm{poly}(n)\cdot M^{\mathcal{O}(1/\log \delta)} \text{ time, where } \delta = n/\log M; \text{ corollary: } \mathrm{poly}(n)\cdot M^{o(1)} \text{ when } M=2^{o(n)}
results.quote: There exists a deterministic algorithm that, given an integer n and a set \(S\subseteq\{1,\dots,M\}\) of size n such that nM<2^n-1, runs in time \(\mathrm{poly}(n)\cdot M^{\mathcal{O}(1/\mathrm{log}\delta)}\) and returns two distinct subsets of S with the same sum, where \(\delta=\delta(n,M):=n/\mathrm{log}M\) is the density of the instance.

results.bound: No \(2^{o(n/\log n)}\) time algorithm under Hypothesis 1; no \(\mathrm{poly}(n)\cdot M^{o(1/\log n)}\) time algorithm
results.quote: Under Hypothesis 1, there is no \(2^{o(n/\log n)}\) time algorithm that solves Pigeonhole Equal Subset Sum. Moreover, there is no \(\mathrm{poly}(n)\cdot M^{o(1/\log n)}\) time algorithm for PESS (even for \(\delta=n^{1/2+o(1)}\)).

results.bound: \tilde{\mathcal{O}}(2^{n/4}) \text{ time with success probability } \Omega(n^{-2}) \text{ for } M=\Theta(2^n)
results.quote: Let \(M=\Theta\left(2^n\right)\). There exists a deterministic algorithm that given a set A of n random integers sampled uniformly from the set {1,...,M}, finds distinct \(X,Y\subseteq A\) such that \(\Sigma(X)=\Sigma(Y)\) with probability \(\Omega\left(n^{-2}\right)\) in \(\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(2^{n/4})\) time.

results.bound: \tilde{\mathcal{O}}(2^{n/4}) \text{ time with success probability } \Omega(1) \text{ for } M=\Theta(2^n), M=pqr, p,q=\Theta(M^{1/4})
results.quote: Let the modulus \(M=\Theta\left(2^n\right)\), where M=pqr, \(p,q=\Theta\left(M^{1/4}\right)\) and p, q, and r are pairwise co-prime integers. There exists a deterministic algorithm that given a set A of n random modular integers sampled uniformly from Z_M, finds distinct \(X,Y\subseteq A\) such that \(\Sigma(X)\equiv_M\Sigma(Y)\) with probability \(\Omega\left(1\right)\) in \(\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(2^{n/4})\) time.
